item.title: A 0.8B Model, 4GB VRAM, Turned Into a Decision Engine: I Reconciled the Two Number Sets in Unsloth's New Feature
item.description: Unsloth added a 'Decision model' capability to its fine-tuning stack: turn a small LLM like Qwen3.5 0.8B into an engine that emits option probabilities only, trainable in 4GB VRAM. Their own X post carries two sets of numbers (20.7%->74.3% and 30-37%->78%); I reconciled both against the official docs line by line. They are two different baselines that align once you split them. Includes a full-model VRAM/time table and a reproduction trap (start r=16, reproduce with r=64).

item.title: Mistral Large 4 'Le Chonk': Spec Check — 1T Parameters, 49B Active, 512K Context, Open Weights Late October
item.description: Mistral shipped Large 4 (Le Chonk) on 2026-10-06: 1T params, 49B active, natively multimodal, API live now, open weights late October. I checked every circulating claim against primary sources: the '1M context' that got quoted everywhere measures 512K in the live API; the $0.68/$2.09 per-M pricing is a curl from my own machine against the public endpoint; the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 38 ties GPT-6 Luna. RL is still running — this is a preview, not the final model.

item.title: SelfSearch: Letting Agents Rewrite Their Own Prompts — Matching Codex for $4.03
item.description: SelfSearch (arXiv 2609.37968): without any downstream reward, agents rewrite their own instructions/tools/procedures using records of prior self-modifications, and a $4.03 search cost yields a harness that solves 82.0% of Terminal-Bench 2.1 — matching Codex, the top of a public nine-harness comparison. The extreme version of prompt evolution.

item.title: Vercel's Inbound Sales Agent: The Prompt Grew From 125 to 1,000 Lines, Then Got Cut to 14 Rules
item.description: Vercel COO post-mortem: the inbound sales agent's prompt grew from 125 to 1,000 lines before the team split it into 14 deterministic rules plus 'the model only does judgment' — running a unicorn's entire inbound for roughly $1,000/year. A subtraction methodology for prompt engineering.
